newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: World Bank backs Bangladesh's plea for IMF loan.
newsitem.headline: World Bank backs Bangladesh's plea for IMF loan.

text.p: A senior World Bank official on Wednesday endorsed Bangladesh's plea for $600 million in balance of payments support from the International Monetary Fund (IMF), saying the money would help Dhaka improve economic management.

"It is a very sound precautionary move when foreign exchange reserves are under pressure. It seems a wise and desirable thing," the bank's Dhaka mission chief, Pierre Landel-Mills, told a news conference.
"The IMF already brings in advice along with assistance which could be an additional support for Bangladesh to improve its economic management...this organisation has enormous expertise," he said.

Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria told reporters earlier this month that the government would soon open negotiations with the IMF, a specialised agency of the United Nations which provides funds to member countries with balance of payments problems.
Landel-Mills said any negotiation with the IMF would be a "good signal" for foreign investors.

"Investors always prefer countries having agreement with IMF. They want to see inflation remain under check and forex reserves stable so that they don't have to face tough exchange rules," he said. "It (an agreement with the IMF) is a seal of good housekeeping."

Bangladesh has received balance of payment support from the IMF twice before, but only after agreeing to follow tough economic programmes. The last IMF package, totalling $430 million in soft loans, ended in 1993.
Official figures at end of September put Bangladesh's foreign exchange reserves at $1.97 billion.
